functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by non-permeabilized anti-FLAG staining (L3). Function NOT MEASURED in the cited clips.
rationale: The canonical NRG1 type I sequence has no signal peptide and the N-terminus (pos 1, M) is directly extracellular (EC 1-242). L3 explicitly confirms via non-permeabilized immunostaining that the N-terminal FLAG tag of the full-length membrane-anchored NRG1 type III construct is displayed on the cell surface. Because the N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus of this single-pass type I topology, insert_after_residue=0 (prepend) is the only possible junction; residue_after is M (pos 1). L9, L10/L11/L12, and L5/L6 provide convergent corroboration across human and zebrafish NRG1 isoforms. Full-length NRG1 type III (700 aa) cloned into p3xFlag-Myc-24 with 3xFLAG at the N-terminus (L2); non-permeabilized anti-FLAG immunostaining of transfected cells confirmed the N-terminal tag is displayed on the extracellular face (L3). The canonical type I sequence (640 aa) has no signal peptide and the same type I topology (EC 1-242), so the N-terminus is directly extracellular. Multiple additional ledger lines (L9: two HA tags at N-terminus of NRG1 used in myelination studies; L10/L11/L12: N-terminal HA on CRD-NRG1 in transgenic mice; L5/L6: mCherry near N-terminus of zebrafish NRG1Iβ1 with confirmed surface localization) all corroborate N-terminal tagging of full-length membrane-bound NRG1 constructs.

rationale: The signal peptide spans residues 1-27 (authoritative landmark); the mature N-terminus begins at residue 28 (R). Wild-type mouse Smo was tagged at the N terminus with YFP or the SNAP tag in the pCS2+ vector (full-length, membrane-anchored construct). The tag was placed C-terminal to the signal sequence. YFP-Smo cells showed surface-exposed Smo by non-permeabilized anti-YFP staining before and after Shh addition. Multiple independent studies (L4/L5/L6/L7: Nluc; L8: FLAG-SNAP; L10: FLAG; L12: YFP; L13: HA/Flag) all place tags at the same N-terminal extracellular junction.
